evidence: createApp builds InMemoryProductRepository/InMemoryOrderRepository and the services: dependency setup, which belongs in infrastructure

GET /orders and POST /orders/:id/:action use isOrderStatus to check query and path parameters and return 400 for bad input: validation at the HTTP boundary
sendError turns DomainError into a 400 and anything else into a 500: transport error handling
startServer reads process.env.PORT and calls listen: server startup belongs in infrastructure
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/HttpServer.ts passes. Everything in it is infrastructure work: the HTTP adapter, request parsing and validation, mapping errors to HTTP status codes, wiring up concrete repositories and services, and starting the server. The business operations are left to the application services (CatalogueService.addProduct/listProducts, OrderService.placeOrder/listOrders/cancelOrder/advanceOrder). The isOrderStatus guard and the check that rejects 'placed' as a URL action only decide which inputs the transport accepts. They do not decide whether an order may move between statuses, which is left to OrderService/domain. sendError only translates DomainError and other errors into HTTP responses, which is transport work. One borderline point: the route handler lists the allowed actions itself, which is close to business knowledge. It is still input validation at the HTTP boundary, so it is not a misplaced responsibility.
